title: A trampoline
description:
Build the bytes of a hook trampoline for a function in your own program: the stolen instructions, then a jump back.

```
target 0x1000: 48 83 EC 28 | 48 8B D9 | ...
need 5 bytes for a jmp -> steal 7 (two whole instructions)
trampoline: 48 83 EC 28 48 8B D9 E9 <back to 0x1007>
patched target: E9 <to hook> 90 90
```
hints: Reuse your jump encoder from the first project of this milestone (lesson 4.04).
Stealing half an instruction breaks the code; that is why you need the instruction lengths (milestone 5's disassembler gives them).
requirements: Given the lengths of the first instructions, steal whole instructions until at least 5 bytes.
The trampoline is the stolen bytes and a `jmp` back to just after them.
The target gets a `jmp` to the hook, with `NOP`s filling the rest of the stolen bytes.
Refuse when a stolen instruction is relative (a `call` or `jmp`), since it would need fixing.
stretch: Fix up a stolen `call rel32` by recomputing its displacement for its new address.
